messages:
Ellen (finance): Quick announcement: updated vendor approval matrix and a new "low-touch" path for trial/POC tools. Please skim and action if you own subscriptions. Full doc + examples: https://docs.redwood.internal/approval-matrix-2026 :loudspeaker:
Ravi (procurement): TL;DR: 1) p-card single charge cap stays $1,000 (exceptions via #help-procurement). 2) New approval matrix below — it replaces ad-hoc email approvals. 3) Low-touch path for trials under $600/yr (single signoff by team lead, no vendor profile required unless they handle PII).
Noelle (security): Important: anything that stores or processes customer data (PII/PHI) is NOT eligible for low-touch. Mark the intake field "handles_customer_data" and we'll pick it up. Security review SLA for standard vendors: 3 business days; expedited = 24-48hrs depending on load.
Tom (eng): Can you paste the new approval matrix here? Easier to decide how to classify things.
Ravi (procurement): Sure — short matrix snippet (use the intake options exactly):

```
# approval matrix (summary)
- low_touch: monthly<=50 AND annual_est<=600 AND handles_customer_data=no -> team_lead_signoff
- standard: monthly<=500 AND annual_est<=6000 AND handles_customer_data=no -> procurement_review
- elevated: annual_est>6000 OR multi-year OR handles_customer_data=yes -> procurement+legal+security
- emergency: expedite_flag=yes -> triage in #help-procurement (attach justification)
```

Ellen (finance): A few process notes: 1) Low-touch signoffs should still include owner_email and a short justification (1 line). 2) Procurement will retroactively create vendor profiles for tools that become standard after a pilot. 3) Noncompliant invoicing may be delayed.
expense-bot: Notice: procurement intake schema updated at 08:30 UTC. New fields: handles_customer_data, low_touch_eligible, approval_path.
Maya (ops): For marketplace or cloud-billed add-ons, which column indicates the billed entity? We get mixed invoices.
Ravi (procurement): Add the vendor_name exactly as on the invoice and add "billed_through" with values like AWS, GCP, Stripe. Procurement will normalize during vendor-profile creation.
Tom (eng): Example: we have a monitoring plugin billed $15/mo via AWS marketplace but the vendor is "MetricWidgets Inc". Low-touch eligible?
Noelle (security): Likely low-touch if it never touches customer data and annual<600 and no infra-level access. But if it needs cross-account IAM roles, mark for procurement review.
Ellen (finance): A couple more examples to help triage teams quickly:

```
# examples
- Trial analytics tool: $0 -> low_touch (add estimated monthly if converting)
- Auth provider (SSO): $200/mo -> elevated (handles_customer_data=yes)
- Backup appliance support: $700/mo -> standard -> procurement_review
```

Ravi (procurement): Operational notes: 1) If a vendor is flagged as "elevated" we'll automatically add legal and security reviewers and set a 5-business-day SLA. 2) Teams can request an expedite but include a rollback/backout plan if the vendor introduces risk.
Maya (ops): For launches, what's the fastest route to get a vendor approved?
Ravi (procurement): Use the intake -> mark expedite-> post a short note in #help-procurement tagging @Ravi and include expected go-live date, owner_email, and a 2-line risk mitigation. We'll triage and can often turn around in 48 hours for non-PII tools.
Tom (eng): Thanks. One ask: can procurement provide a CSV mapping of approved low-touch vendors so we can filter them from our billing alerts?
Ravi (procurement): We'll publish a weekly "low-touch whitelist" CSV and a canonical_vendor_id mapping starting next Monday. Until then, please tag exports with cost_center and project.
Noelle (security): Also: if teams plan to store customer logs externally for debugging, even if vendor is cheap, mark handles_customer_data=yes. We'll consult on retention/encryption.
Ellen (finance): Final: action items: teams, update intake for any recurring subscriptions by 2026-05-05 COB; use the new fields; team leads approve low-touch requests; post exceptions in #help-procurement. We'll host a 20-min office hours on Friday for Q&A. :calendar:
